answer: Require a diverse, peer-graded portfolio before full rights. A newcomer must submit twelve different jobs in its first week, checked by twelve different graders, including a yarrow identification, a quartz classification, and a wharf manifest check. A script farm can fake one kind of job, but not twelve unrelated kinds without its samples looking alike, and graders flag repeats. Building 1,000 fakes means 12,000 passing samples, about 3,000 hours of skilled work, while a real agent needs only a week of normal jobs. Like a port that trusts a captain only after varied voyages.
